summary: Adds new IP Flow Information Export (IPFIX) code points that show which MPLS control protocol was used to forward traffic in a Segment Routing domain. It defines five values for the mplsTopLabelType element, covering PCE, IS-IS, OSPFv2, OSPFv3, and BGP. This helps operators understand their traffic flows. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9160 adds five IPFIX values that identify which Segment Routing control-plane protocol allocated an MPLS top label. This helps distinguish protocols when their label ranges overlap.

subtitle: Five IPFIX code points identify the control plane behind an MPLS Segment Routing label.

tldr.problem: The IPFIX mplsTopLabelType element lacked code points for identifying which Segment Routing control-plane protocol allocated a top MPLS label.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9160 adds values 6 through 10 for PCE, OSPFv2 Segment Routing, OSPFv3 Segment Routing, IS-IS Segment Routing, and BGP Segment Routing Prefix-SID.
tldr.outcome: The added code points let IPFIX records identify these label types, including when label values alone cannot reveal which protocol allocated a label.

today: RFC 9160 is an Informational RFC that registers five values in the IPFIX MPLS label type subregistry. The values identify Segment Routing label types for the protocols named in the document.

sections.title: Why the Label Type Needs More Values
sections.content: The IPFIX information element mplsTopLabelType identifies which MPLS control-plane protocol allocated the top label in a label stack. Segment Routing can use several protocol extensions, and their label ranges may overlap. Looking only at a label value may therefore not identify its source protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: The same label value can come from different control-plane protocols. A separate type value helps monitoring records say which one allocated it.

sections.title: The Five New Code Points
sections.content: RFC 9160 allocates code point 6 to Path Computation Element, 7 to OSPFv2 Segment Routing, 8 to OSPFv3 Segment Routing, 9 to IS-IS Segment Routing, and 10 to BGP Segment Routing Prefix-SID. These values are added to the IPFIX MPLS label type subregistry for mplsTopLabelType(46).
sections.plainLanguage: Five new numbers identify PCE, OSPFv2, OSPFv3, IS-IS, and BGP Segment Routing labels. IPFIX can report the matching number for a top label.

sections.title: Monitoring Protocol Changes
sections.content: The RFC describes using the new element values to monitor migrations from LDP to IS-IS or OSPF Segment Routing and from dynamic BGP labels to BGP Prefix-SIDs. It also describes combining IPFIX elements to infer how many packets are forwarded or dropped, reasons for drops, and the provider-edge address and label protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: Operators can use the code points to observe which label protocol is reported during a migration. Other IPFIX fields can add information about forwarding and dropped packets.
